title: Urinary Peptide Panel to Predict Necessity of Repeated Transurethral Resection of Bladder Tumour
summary:
One treatment option for non–muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) is the transurethral resection of the bladder tumor (TURBT). During this procedure, all visible tumors are removed and tissue samples are obtained for pathological analysis. Due to the risk of residual tumor after the initial TURBT, current treatment guidelines recommend a repeat resection (re-TURBT) 2 to 6 weeks after the first resection for certain cases of NMIBC. Although repeat TURBT is considered a minor procedure, non-invasive analyses may offer an opportunity to avoid unnecessary repeat resections, i.e., surgical procedures.

The aim of this study is to develop a urine-based biomarker panel composed of proteins as a non-invasive alternative for predicting residual bladder cancer after an initial TURBT for NMIBC. Such a non-invasive alternative could prevent unnecessary repeat resections and thereby reduce the risks associated with repeat surgery as well as the costs of the procedure and the associated hospital stay.

interventions.name: prospective collection and analysis of urine specimen of patients who need a re-TURBT (repeat transurethral resection of a bladder tumor) due to a non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) (study period: 2026-2028)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Initial TURBT for non–muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder (NMIBC)
Minimum age of 18 years
Informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Macroscopically incomplete initial TURBT (according to the surgeon’s assessment)
Concomitant carcinoma in situ / urothelial carcinoma of the upper urinary tract
Muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladder (MIBC)
Recurrent urothelial carcinoma of the urinary bladde
